messages:
maya: quick review: confirmation modal for deleting eval results reads: `Delete results? This action cannot be undone.` PM worries it's too blunt and users might accidentally lose important eval history. can we soften wording and offer alternatives like archive?

oliver: i saw a few users on support ask if deleting results also removes snapshots and logs. copy should clarify what is deleted. also need to confirm retention/backups policies link.

nina: accessibility + tone notes: buttons should be explicit about outcome. avoid using `Delete` alone on the primary CTA; prefer `Discard results` or `Permanently discard results`. also avoid color-only cues—add clear text.

sam: propose this flow: 1) Title: `Discard evaluation results?` 2) Body: short sentence clarifying permanence and what gets removed. 3) Secondary link: `Archive results instead` 4) Checkbox (optional): `Also delete associated snapshots and logs` (unchecked by default) 5) Primary CTA: `Discard results` (danger) 6) Secondary CTA: `Cancel`

maya: yes to checkbox. can we make the checkbox copy actionable: `Also delete associated snapshots & logs (cannot be recovered)` so it's explicit. but keep the modal from feeling accusatory.

design-bot: suggested concise modal copy (engineer-ready strings):

Title: "Discard evaluation results?"
Body: "This will permanently remove the selected evaluation results. Snapshots and logs are not deleted unless you check the option below. This action cant be undone."
Checkbox line: "Also delete associated snapshots & logs (cannot be recovered)"
Primary button: "Discard results"
Secondary button: "Cancel"
Alternative action link (muted): "Archive results instead"
Screen-reader alert: "You are about to discard evaluation results. This will permanently remove the selected results. Snapshots and logs will remain unless you select the delete snapshots checkbox. Press discard to confirm or cancel to go back."

nina: SR text tweak: spell out `cannot be recovered` instead of `cannot be undone` for clarity. and use sentence case. also set aria-describedby to match body so SR reads full context.

oliver: small legal/product nit: if we include the backup policy link, make it open in a new tab and mark `noopener`. copy suggestion for inline link: `See our retention and backup policy` (muted small link).

sam: also add microcopy for the danger confirmation step if users check the checkbox: show a second confirm step `Type DISCARD to confirm` when the checkbox is selected, to prevent accidental loss for large eval suites. do we all agree?

maya: i think that second-step is good for >1000-result deletions. can we make it conditional: if selection_count > 1000, show typed confirm. otherwise just the checkbox and discard click.

design-bot: developer strings for typed-confirm state:

Typed confirm prompt (visible only for large selections): "Type DISCARD to confirm permanent deletion of {n} results."
Confirm input aria-label: "Confirm deletion by typing DISCARD"
Error state copy: "Text did not match. Deletion cancelled."

nina: final accessibility checklist for engineers: 1) focus trap in modal 2) primary button has aria-disabled until user interaction rules satisfied (typed confirm if shown) 3) checkbox is keyboard reachable and has clear label 4) aria-live polite for success/failure toast messages 5) high contrast for danger button

maya: thanks team. i'll push these strings into the copy doc and add a small mock. tagging eng to implement conditional typed-confirm and retention link behavior. :pray:
